name: al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi (compiler)
bio: Al-Mufaddal ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi, of the tribe of Dabbah, was an Arabic philologist and transmitter of old poetry who lived in Kufa in the eighth century and died around 780. He is remembered as one of the great collectors of pre-Islamic verse.

He is best known for the anthology that bears his name, the Mufaddaliyat, a collection of about 126 odes and fragments by pre-Islamic and early Islamic poets. The Arabic text of the odes held here is given in the Wikisource transcription, in its work page.
